entities.summary:
Frans van Schooten Jr. was a Dutch mathematician who popularized the analytic geometry of René Descartes. Born into a prominent Amsterdam family, he studied law and mathematics, eventually becoming a professor of mathematics at the University of Utrecht in 1648. Van Schooten's translation of La Géométrie, accompanied by extensive commentaries, became the standard reference for European scientists and mathematicians. His work played a crucial role in the development of calculus and the understanding of spatial relationships.

The translation of La Géométrie, which took several years to complete, was a groundbreaking achievement that made Descartes' work accessible to a broader audience. Van Schooten's commentaries, written in collaboration with Johannes Hudde, Johan de Witt, and Hendrik van Heuraet, provided a deeper understanding of the mathematical concepts. This translation and commentary set the stage for the development of calculus and its applications in physics and engineering.

The influence of Van Schooten's work can be seen in the work of later mathematicians and scientists, who built upon his translations and commentaries. His legacy extends beyond the field of mathematics, as his work contributed to the broader understanding of the scientific revolution of the 17th century.

Despite his significant contributions, Van Schooten's personal life remains relatively unknown. He died on May 29, 1660, at the age of 43, leaving behind a lasting impact on the world of mathematics and science.

Van Schooten's translation of La Géométrie is still studied today, and his commentaries continue to provide valuable insights into the mathematical concepts of Descartes' time.

Van Schooten's legacy is a testament to the power of translation and collaboration in the advancement of human knowledge.
